LENGTH_EXPOSURE_FINDING.observation: DSMC selects 1.53x the post-template tokens of Random-K (1,459,218 vs 950,783; mean 539 vs 351). ALL four target-aware selectors skew long relative to Random (1.33x-1.53x); DSMC is the most extreme but not an outlier among them. Random is the shortest on every statistic (median, p90, max, n>2048). Source entropy shows the same ordering: Random 1.201 > LESS 1.090 > First-RR 1.037 > Second-RR 0.977 > DSMC 0.833, i.e. DSMC is the most concentrated (70% flan_v2 vs Random 39%).
LENGTH_EXPOSURE_FINDING.why_this_matters: The BBH arm carries no Random-K-LengthMatched control (the MMLU arm has one). At a FIXED example budget K=2707, a 1.53x token advantage means DSMC-trained adapters see ~1.5x more supervised tokens than Random-trained ones, so a downstream DSMC>Random result could be partly a token-budget effect rather than a targeting effect. Note the MMLU arm found Random >= DSMC, so this confound would work AGAINST the MMLU finding, not for it.
LENGTH_EXPOSURE_FINDING.decision_status: DECIDED (advice_0810_2): add Random-K-LengthMatched as a PRE-REGISTERED SECONDARY SENSITIVITY CONTROL -- not a sixth primary selector. Done now, before any BBH adapter accuracy exists, so it cannot be outcome-driven. The primary comparison set is unchanged.
LENGTH_EXPOSURE_FINDING.cost_if_added: +6 adapters (3 draws x 2 seeds) = +6 evals x 111.4 min + ~1.5 h train = ~12.6 GPU-h
LENGTH_EXPOSURE_FINDING.do_not: no method was changed on the basis of this diagnostic
LENGTH_EXPOSURE_FINDING.RETRACTED_WORDING: I wrote 'DSMC adapters would see ~1.5x more supervised tokens'. That is WRONG and is retracted. The measured field is post-template SEQUENCE tokens (full input_ids), not loss-bearing labels. Under the llama2 template the prompt is MASKED, so only the assistant continuation is supervised -- on a 300-candidate probe that is ~18.5% of the sequence. A 1.53x sequence-token ratio therefore does NOT imply a 1.53x supervised-token ratio.
LENGTH_EXPOSURE_FINDING.CORRECT_WORDING: DSMC has ~1.5x greater post-template SEQUENCE-TOKEN exposure than Random-K at fixed K=2707. The difference in loss-bearing supervised tokens is measured separately in candidate_length_cache_manifest.json and the phase-B recomputation; it must not be assumed equal to the sequence ratio.
LENGTH_EXPOSURE_FINDING.ratio_is_not_a_tail_artifact: Subtracting the tokens lost to the 2048 cutoff, retained sequence exposure is still (1459218-28734)/(950783-2326) = 1.51x, so the gap is not caused by a few over-long outliers.

AUTHORITATIVE_MEASUREMENT.supersedes: the earlier numbers (47,438 / 268,850) were computed from a cache that hand-rebuilt a single [INST] u [/INST] a turn. A message-structure audit found 24,628/270,679 candidates (9.10%, all oasst1) are MULTI-TURN, where LlamaFactory wraps every user turn and supervises every assistant turn. Those numbers are therefore SUPERSEDED -- though they were only slightly off, see below.

AUTHORITATIVE_MEASUREMENT.FINDING_SURVIVES: sequence ratio 1.5050 (was 1.5082 provisionally) and label ratio 0.1764 (unchanged). The effect was real; it is now measured on the correct base.
AUTHORITATIVE_MEASUREMENT.CORRECT_TERMINOLOGY: DSMC exposes the model to 1.51x as many POST-CUTOFF SEQUENCE POSITIONS but only 0.18x as many LOSS-BEARING LABEL POSITIONS per epoch as Random-K. Do NOT call sequence tokens "GPU cost" (batches pad to the longest member, so unpadded sums are not FLOPs). Do NOT call label positions "amount of supervised signal" (the loss ignores -100 then takes a token-normalized mean CE, so Nx positions is not Nx gradient signal).
AUTHORITATIVE_MEASUREMENT.MECHANISM_STATUS: CONSISTENT WITH format matching, NOT a demonstrated mechanism. DSMC selects long prompts with very short answers (mean 528 sequence positions, mean 17.5 label positions = 3%; median 9; 334/2707 with <=2), i.e. classification/multiple-choice/extractive data, while Random draws free-form generation (28%). BBH's own targets ARE single tokens like "(C)", "14", "Yes" -- consistent, but the causal claim is not established.
